issues.body: Section 1 says that because the defining symbols first appear in sparq's whole-tree import commit, the three branches 'were merged upstream, before the snapshot was taken.' `git log -S` in this repository proves only that the imported snapshot contains those symbols; it says nothing about whether the named upstream branches were merged, abandoned, or contained additional changes. The document itself acknowledges that branch tips were unreachable, says commit-level completeness is unproved, and asks the maintainer in section 8 whether the branches were merged. Consequently, the unconditional outcome 'all three branches are DROP — subsumed' is not established by the evidence. This matters operationally because deleting an upstream branch could discard work outside each headline capability.
issues.fix_hint: Either obtain and compare the three upstream branch tips against import revision `1e555b10` before issuing branch-level DROP verdicts, or narrow the record consistently to 'headline capability already present; branch-level port/drop deferred pending upstream comparison/maintainer confirmation.' Remove the claim that the branches were merged before the snapshot unless supported by upstream history, and align the outcome line, verdict table, and section 8 with the weaker capability-level conclusion.
issues.title: DROP verdict relies on an unverified upstream-merge inference

verdict.summary: The record is careful in several places to disclose that upstream branch tips were unavailable and that only capability-level evidence was checked. However, its central DROP/subsumed conclusion is presented more strongly than that evidence permits, and section 1 makes an unsupported historical inference that directly conflicts with the stated limitation and open questions. The cited in-tree tests support the presence of the headline capabilities, but cannot establish that each upstream branch was merged before the snapshot or that no branch work remains to port.
